Consistent with the historical seasonality of the business, we anticipate 2016 profitability and profitability growth to be heavily concentrated in the second half of the year. 
 We implemented our new ERP system in our international distributor businesses in May 2015, which joins our North American wholesale business, excluding prAna, and the majority of our global supply chain operations onto our new platform. The next planned phase of our global information systems and infrastructure initiatives is to transition our Japan subsidiary to our new ERP system.

attrs.management_says: No explicit explanation for 2015 receivables movement in evidence; general references to seasonality and ERP implementation (E30, E49).
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 8.0% ($27.6M) vs revenue +10.7%; DSO improved from 60 to 58 days (E23). Quarterly: Q1 AR +1% (DSO 53→48), Q2 AR -3% (DSO 57→47), Q3 AR +15.5% (DSO 62→63), Q4 AR +8% (DSO 46→48) (E25-E28). Pattern shows AR growing slower than revenue overall, consistent with healthy demand.

attrs.management_says: No explanation for 2015 operating cash flow decline in provided MD&A excerpts. Prior year (2014) decline attributed to inventory and AR increases (E47). Forward-looking risks mention weather, order cancellations, ERP transition (E30, E31).
attrs.numbers_show: Operating cash flow fell 49% to $95.1M from $185.8M while net income rose 27% to $174.3M (E6, E16, E17, E24). The $90.7M CFO drop vs $37.1M net income rise implies ~$128M adverse working capital/non-cash changes. AR increased $27.6M; current liabilities fell $7M; current assets fell $16.6M overall, suggesting inventory/other current assets declined (source of cash), so other factors (e.g., tax payments, non-current working capital, ERP disruption) likely drove the CFO decline.

attrs.reason: Operating cash flow fell 49% (E6, E17, E24) while net income rose 27%; the provided MD&A excerpts (E30, E47, E49) do not quantify working capital movements (inventory, payables) or ERP cash outflows to explain the divergence.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 49% decline in operating cash flow despite higher net income reflects a substantial inventory build to support the 13.7% Q3 revenue surge and fall seasonal shipments (E27, E49), compounded by cash outflows from the May 2015 ERP implementation in international distributor businesses (E30).

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Management's general references to seasonality and ERP implementation (E30, E49) are consistent with the reported receivables pattern: receivables grew 8.0% versus 10.7% revenue growth, improving DSO from 60 to 58 days (E23). Quarterly data shows receivables growing slower than revenue in Q1 (+1% vs +12.9%), Q2 (-3% vs +17.3%), and Q4 (+8% vs +3.3%), with a seasonal surge in Q3 (+15.5% vs +13.7%) (E25-E28). The May 2015 ERP implementation (E30) aligns with the timing of Q3/Q4 changes. The numbers corroborate the seasonal pattern and show no deterioration in collections.

The 2014 MD&A attributed a CFO decline to inventory and AR increases (E47), but the 2015 MD&A excerpts (E30, E31) only mention forward-looking risks (weather, ERP transition) without addressing the 2015 CFO drop. A full reconciliation requires a detailed working capital breakdown (inventory, accounts payable, tax payments) that is not present in the evidence pack.
